questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: HU-unisport was super good and has a lot of different possibilities for sport activities. And is pretty cheap. But you have to be ready for sign up on the relaseday cause the courses are booked out pretty quick. Also it's a good opportunity to meet local german students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Follow Louisa Neubauer on instagram and join some Fridays for future demos. That was super fun and a good expirience to see how that's done in Berlin compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out to parks, clubs, restaurants, the lakes, museums, fleamarkets fx on Arkonaplatz, RAW Gelände or Boxhagener Platz.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Some prefer speaking german but they are super nice. The social part of the uni is not a lot unless you go on field trips. Unisport is easier.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: But some things supprised me. Fx they go on holidays directly after the teaching ends and wait to do the exams before last minute when you forgot everything instead of doing "læseferie" directly and then holiday. You can do it as you like but it might be diffucult if it is group work.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They were all pretty motivated to do the studies.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to get housing in the city instead of Adlershof near the campus.

If you wanna get to know danish people at some point the danish church "Christianskirken" does a lot of cool events for young peaople who just moved to the city. Fx. "meet and eat" where you eat nice foods and drink beers together.

Make sure that your courses are beginner courses so you are not already behind on some consensual stuff from the beginning. There are not a lot of other exchange students on the Bachelor so you will have plenty of challenges following along all of the consensual practical stuff compared to the germans.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The students dont always know each other in the courses to begin with but its a great opportunity to arrenge something social for the group.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Outside perspective on the daily life back home and realising how many different ways there is to do the thing you just consider "normal" or take forgiven.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I didn't that the other students didn't write the exams before last minute after a long break.
